newsitem.title: USA: Calif. voters turn against securities measure-poll.
newsitem.headline: Calif. voters turn against securities measure-poll.

text.p: California voters appear to be turning against a ballot initiative that would make it easier for investors to sue corporations for securities fraud, according to an opinion poll released Wednesday.

The independent Field Institute of San Francisco said its poll results showed "a strong tide of opposition has surfaced" against the measure, known as Proposition 211, which will be on the ballot in California next Tuesday.
After being read a summary of the measure, 54 percent of likely voters said they would vote against Proposition 211 while 28 percent were in favour and 18 percent undecided.
The measure was leading in the last Field Poll in early October when 39 percent of likely voters supported the proposal and 31 opposed it, with 30 percent undecided.
The survey of 824 likely California voters was carried out October 25-28 and had a margin of error of 3.5 percentage points.
Proposition 211 would make company executives personally liable for fraud and shift the burden of proof in fraud cases to the person being sued.
Backers of the proposal say it punishes white collar cheaters who defraud people out of their pension savings.

Opponents, including many Silicon Valley business executives, say it could make California state courts a magnet for class action lawsuits and send stock prices reeling. They say lawyers filing the suits stand to gain the most from the initiative.
The fight over the initiative has been one of the most expensive in the nation, with opponents spending more than $30 million to fight the measure.
